result:
I’d make empathy involuntary—not optional, not selective, not limited to people who look, think, or live like us.

If every person could truly feel, even briefly, the weight of another person’s fear, hunger, humiliation, or grief as if it were their own, most cruelty would become unbearable to commit. Wars, exploitation, neglect, indifference—many of the world’s worst things survive because other people’s pain is easy to ignore.

Not kindness as a rule. Not morality as obedience. Just understanding so immediate that harming another would feel like harming yourself.
